title: Lymphatic & Immune System
shortDescription: Lymph, lymph nodes, the spleen and thymus, and the innate vs. adaptive immunity split — an introductory, exam-oriented chapter.
genZNote: Your body's drainage system doubles as its security team.

structures.name: Lymph nodes
structures.description: Small bean-shaped structures along lymphatic vessels.
structures.function: Filter lymph and house immune cells that respond to pathogens.

structures.name: Spleen
structures.description: Organ in the upper left abdomen.
structures.function: Filters blood, recycles old red blood cells, and houses immune cells.

structures.name: Thymus
structures.description: Gland in the chest, most active in childhood.

structures.name: Tonsils
structures.description: Lymphatic tissue at the back of the throat.
structures.function: Trap and help destroy pathogens entering through the mouth or nose.

structures.name: Lymphatic vessels
structures.description: Network of thin vessels running alongside blood vessels.
structures.function: Return leaked fluid (lymph) from tissues back to the bloodstream.

comparisons.distinction: Innate immunity is fast, general, and present from birth; adaptive immunity is slower, pathogen-specific, and builds memory.
T cells mature in the thymus and directly attack infected cells; B cells mature in bone marrow and produce antibodies.
Lymph nodes filter lymph fluid; the spleen filters blood.

questions.prompt: Which type of immunity is pathogen-specific and builds long-term memory?
questions.explanation: Adaptive immunity is slower to activate but is pathogen-specific and forms memory cells for faster future responses.
optionNotes: Fast and general, but not pathogen-specific and has no memory.

questions.prompt: Which organ filters blood (not lymph) and recycles old red blood cells?
questions.explanation: The spleen filters blood and recycles old red blood cells; lymph nodes filter lymph fluid instead.
optionNotes: Traps pathogens at the throat, doesn't filter blood.

questions.explanation: T cells mature in the thymus (hence the name “T” cell). B cells mature in bone marrow.
optionNotes: Filters blood, isn't the maturation site for T cells.
This is where B cells mature.
Filter lymph, but aren't the maturation site.

sections.heading: Lymphatic Structures
bullets: Lymph — the clear fluid that leaks from blood vessels into tissues and is collected by the lymphatic system.
Lymphatic vessels — carry lymph back toward the bloodstream, running alongside blood vessels.
Lymph nodes — small, bean-shaped structures that filter lymph and house immune cells that attack pathogens.
Spleen — filters blood, recycles old red blood cells, and stores immune cells.
Thymus — matures T-cells (see Endocrine chapter for its hormonal role).
Tonsils — lymphatic tissue in the throat that helps trap pathogens entering via the mouth/nose.

sections.heading: White Blood Cells
sections.body: White blood cells (leukocytes) are the immune system's main cellular defenders, circulating in blood and lymph and concentrating at lymph nodes and the spleen to detect and destroy pathogens.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The lymphatic system drains excess tissue fluid back into the blood and works closely with the immune system's lymph nodes, spleen, and thymus to fight infection.
keyFacts: Lymph nodes filter lymph fluid and are packed with immune cells.
The spleen filters blood, not lymph — a commonly tested distinction.
Innate immunity is fast and general; adaptive immunity is slower but specific and has memory.
The thymus matures T-cells and is most active in childhood.
commonConfusion: Lymph nodes filter lymph; the spleen filters blood — students often assume both filter the same fluid.

highYieldFacts: Only adaptive immunity produces immune memory, which is why vaccines work.
The spleen recycles old red blood cells in addition to its immune role.
commonTraps: Don't say lymph nodes filter blood — they filter lymph fluid; the spleen is the one that filters blood.
mustRemember: Lymph nodes → filter lymph. Spleen → filters blood. Thymus → matures T-cells.
Innate = fast/general/no memory. Adaptive = slow/specific/has memory.
